/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 28 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2677 (11)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4304 (22)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1966 (9)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1542 (2)
Baltic Handysize Index: 804 (2)
CAPESIZE
A more positive tone returned to the market today, with sentiment improving across both basins, albeit with a continued divergence in activity levels. The BCI 182 5TC edged up by $202 to $39,039, supported by a busier Pacific, while the Atlantic remained comparatively standoffish despite underlying support. In the Pacific, activity picked up, underpinned by solid cargo volumes and the presence of three miners on C5. Rates firmed modestly, with C5 rising by $0.170 to $13.200. Early offers were reported in the upper $13s, with an operator concluding at $13.50, while miners were seen bidding in the $12.90–$13.00 range against offers in the low $13s, with $13.10 reported by one miner. In the Atlantic, the C3 index held relatively steady, edging up by $0.086 to $33.118. Despite a supportive backdrop, particularly with a tight ballaster list for May loaders, activity remained limited, especially out of South Brazil and West Africa. A notable bid-offer gap persisted on C3, with bids around $32 against offers closer to $34 for end-May dates.
PANAMAX
As the week gets underway, a clear divergence is emerging between the Atlantic and Pacific markets. In the Atlantic, conditions remain largely unchanged from Monday, with a steady flow of tonnage opening in the North Continent and a continued lack of mineral and grain transatlantic stems, leaving the market without meaningful support. Fronthaul sentiment also softened, with weaker fixtures reported out of the US Gulf compared to recent levels. The P2A index declined by $307 to $24,579. In contrast, the Pacific market is maintaining a firmer tone. Market participants report ongoing activity out of Australia and Indonesia, helping to underpin sentiment. Firmer fixtures have been noted, including relatively strong levels achieved for overage tonnage on Indonesian business. The Hui Tong (83,601 2010) open Koh Sichang 25 April was reported fixed for 11/13 months at around $17,250, with some suggesting closer to $17,500, though the charterer remains undisclosed. The P5TC index edged up by $78 to close at $17,695.

Asia
Aeolian (83,748 2012) Hakata 30 April was said to have been fixed but no further details surfaced. Mingwah were reported to have covered in-house their North Pacific requirement for 18 May dates and Oldendorff covered their Vietnam or China clinker requirement to West Africa for 5/10 May, but further details are yet to be heard. Messrs Usiminas were reported to have covered their voyage requirement from East Coast Australia into Brazil for 18/24 May in the upper $18.00’s.
SUPRAMAX
Many felt that it remained a rather positional affair across both the Atlantic and Asian arenas. In the Atlantic whilst some felt that the Continent - Mediterranean had seen a little more demand appearing, the US Gulf was finely balanced. Although positive sentiment remained in the US Gulf some said that fresh enquiry would be required. In Asia, similar to the Atlantic demined eased slightly from the north but rates and interest remained healthy further south. a 57,000 open Gresik was heard fixed for a trip via Indonesia redelivery SE Asia at $21,000. Elsewhere the Indian Ocean was active, the Astro Grumium (61,305 2015) Mombasa 2/4 May was heard fixed basis delivery Durban for a redelivery Vietnam at $22,000 plus $220,000 ballast bonus to Topic. Also, the Eastern Daphne (56,810 2013) open Mombasa was heard fixed for trip via Richards Bay redelivery Vietnam at $16,000. The CMB Jordaens (63,447 2019) open Visakhapatnam 3/5 May was fixed for a coastal to WC India at around $22,000 by Bainbridge. The 11TC average finished at $19,487 up just $18.00.
HANDYSIZE
A north-south divide was seen in the Atlantic as fresh enquiry remained lacking from the Continent-Mediterranean brokers said. The South Atlantic remained relatively stable although little fresh information emerged. Positive sentiment remained in place from the US Gulf, again fixing information was limited. The Asian arena was finely balanced. it surfaced that the Paiwan Diamond (42,846 2026) Penang was heard to have fixed at $17,000 for a run from South Australia with grains to Makassar. Also, a 30,000 was heard fixed for North Vietnam redelivery Singapore with cement at around $13,000, but no further details surfaced. Elsewhere, the Ocean Helios (40,076 2026) open Saldanha Bay 9/19 May was heard fixed for a backhaul trip to the US Gulf at $16,750 with Ultrabulk. The 7TC average closed up slightly by $39 at $14,467.

Market Fundamentals
CISA Daily Crude Steel Production

In the period 11-20 April, crude steel production at Chinese Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills lifted 0.4% from the preceding ten days to 2.1 Mt/day, a year-to-date high and the highest since mid-August last year, according to the industry association. However, output stood 5.3% below the same period last year.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve rallied higher in response to a firmer Pacific market, combined with a tighter south Atlantic market. The biggest move was on the May contract with 35350 paid, followed by the June up to a high of 34000. The May v June spread continued to widen and strengthen with 1750 paid. Q3 was supported on open with volume being paid up to 30600, before being sold back down to 28900. Similarly the trading range on Q4 was 29800-30300 but with sporadic liquidity, whereas the Cal27 traded up to 25900 during the morning session, then sold down to 25550 during the afternoon sell-off. Activity on the Cal28 was limited with 22900 paid, then sold back down to 22650.

PMX
PMX opened slightly higher than yesterday’s close, with good volume seen across the curve. May traded down to a low of 18800 before being paid up to 19600, finishing the day around 19100. Jun saw less movement, trading in a range of 19200–19700 and closing at 19500. Aug was paid at 18800, which saw the Jun/Aug spread trade at 800. Q3 bounced around 18500 to 18900, while Q4 held a tighter range between 17250 and 17400. Further out, Cal27 saw participation today, trading around 14650.

SMX + HANDY
The Smx Asia Index cast doubt over the strength of paper with a modest +10 on the Avg TC. This somewhat set the tone of sellers being more eager to transact, though in the morning session positivity from the bigger vessel sizes largely offset the negative concerns on Smx. Though paper levels dropped quicker in the afternoon session after the Avg 10tc Index continued to slow being just +19 to $17453. May traded from 17750 down to a low of 17050, June 17600 - 17100 whilst the quarters also lost reasonable ground as Q3 printed 16800 - 16350 an Q4 15350 - 15200. The Cal27 saw moderate activity to trade 13000 - 12900 and and the Cal28 traded just one small clip at 12050.

Carbon
EU ETS futures drifted slightly higher on Tuesday ending the day up by around 0.5-0.7% (higher for the further out contracts). Dec 26 was trading around �75.17/T at 16.00 BST at daily volume of just over 16,000. On other contracts liquidity was thin and bid/ask spreads were wide.

Market Fundamentals
CISA Daily Crude Steel Production
In the period 11-20 April, crude steel production at Chinese
Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills lifted 0.4%
from the preceding ten days to 2.1 Mt/day, a year-to-date
high and the highest since mid-August last year, according to
the industry association. However, output stood 5.3% below
the same period last year.
Trading Commentary
Cape Routes
The c5 market moved higher again today as the may
contract traded a few times up at 13.30 where it closed
oﬀered on. The june had some enquiry but not trades to
report, closing valued at 13.10. The c3 also ticked up again
today as the may traded at 33.40 in the morning session,
closing slightly lower valued at 33.25. The june also had alot
of enquiry but no trades reported.
Cape
The Cape FFA curve rallied higher in response to a ﬁrmer
Paciﬁc market, combined with a tighter south Atlantic
market. The biggest move was on the May contract with
35350 paid, followed by the June up to a high of 34000. The
May v June spread continued to widen and strengthen with
1750 paid. Q3 was supported on open with volume being
paid up to 30600, before being sold back down to 28900.
Similarly the trading range on Q4 was 29800-30300 but with
sporadic liquidity, whereas the Cal27 traded up to 25900
during the morning session, then sold down to 25550 during
the afternoon sell-oﬀ. Activity on the Cal28 was limited with
22900 paid, then sold back down to 22650.
PMX
PMX opened slightly higher than yesterday’s close, with good
volume seen across the curve. May traded down to a low of
18800 before being paid up to 19600, ﬁnishing the day
around 19100. Jun saw less movement, trading in a range of
19200–19700 and closing at 19500. Aug was paid at 18800,
which saw the Jun/Aug spread trade at 800. Q3 bounced
around 18500 to 18900, while Q4 held a tighter range
between 17250 and 17400. Further out, Cal27 saw
participation today, trading around 14650.
SMX + HANDY
The Smx Asia Index cast doubt over the strength of paper
with a modest +10 on the Avg TC. This somewhat set the
tone of sellers being more eager to transact, though in the
morning session positivity from the bigger vessel sizes
largely oﬀset the negative concerns on Smx. Though paper
levels dropped quicker in the afternoon session after the Avg
10tc Index continued to slow being just +19 to $17453. May
traded from 17750 down to a low of 17050, June 17600 -
17100 whilst the quarters also lost reasonable ground as Q3
printed 16800 - 16350 an Q4 15350 - 15200. The Cal27 saw
moderate activity to trade 13000 - 12900 and and the Cal28
traded just one small clip at 12050.Cape 180 5TC

Handysize/Supramax Report28th April 2026
63,500 Atlantic: SOFTER      Paciﬁc: FLAT           38,000 Atlantic: FLAT      Paciﬁc: FLAT
Market Comments
ATLANTIC:
In the Handysize Continent market, activity remains subdued with little fresh enquiry thus
far. Fixing levels are at around USD 9,000 for a transatlantic voyage, a similar level to last
week. For the Supramax and Ultramax sizes, rates have held ﬁrm from last week, supported
by a relatively tight tonnage list. We have seen a 63k deadweight vessel ﬁx a trip from ARAG
range to East Coast Mexico on subjects at USD 12,000. In the Handysize Mediterranean
market, rates have remained ﬂat as the week opened with limited fresh enquiries. We saw a
39k deadweight vessel rate a trip from the East Mediterranean to Spore/Japan range at USD
16,000, which is the same rating as last week. We saw a 35k deadweight vessel ﬁx a trip
from Çanakkale to Florida at USD 10,750 (plus USD 150,000 ILOHC). For the larger sizes,
tonnage lists remain long and enquiry limited. Fixing levels are at around USD 10,000 for a
transatlantic voyage, a ﬁrmer level than last week. The Handysize East Coast South America
(ECSA) market is still hot with healthy demand, thus we are continuing to see better rates.
For the Ultramax size, fronthaul numbers are sitting at USD 17,000 + 700k GBB. Meanwhile
in West Africa, there is limited demand and the tonnage list is building. The Handysize US
Gulf market has opened particularly slowly this week as both Owners and Charterers try to
gauge current market direction. Underlying sentiment feels quietly constructive, with
Owners pushing ﬁrmer ideas. There has been limited fresh enquiry, however we suspect
Charterers are keeping some orders oﬀ market until later in the week. Tonnage count
remains stable, possibly marginally tighter than last week. Whereas on the Supramax and
Ultramax US Gulf market it has been a rather quiet start to the week. We are still seeing
some inter-caribs business present but less transatlantic enquiry. Fronthaul orders are
building up for mid May dates with grains especially, but nothing has been concluded yet.
We feel the market is a tick ﬁrmer for the fronthauls as the market aligns closer to the
transatlantic levels which are coming down from the upper 20k levels.
PACIFIC:
The Paciﬁc market was quiet this week. Most prompt cargoes have been covered, but there
are still some spot vessels left. In the Southeast Asian coal market, the India direction was
less hot than last week. A UMX open in Chittagong could not see 20k DOP for an Indo/India
run this week, marking a downward adjustment compared to last week. For the Indo/China
direction, bids for an SMX based in Singapore were around mid 15k, also lower. There are
still a few Indo/Thai cargoes waiting to be covered, with rates showing no signiﬁcant
change. It was heard that a UMX open in the Philippines ﬁxed at 21.5k for an Indo/Thai
run. Aussie cargoes generally felt that tonnage supply was ample. Oﬀers this week
decreased by 1-2k compared to last week. It is currently heard that a UMX open in
Chittagong can see around mid 16k for an Aussie RV, but owners' ideas remain high, with
most owners wanting 18-19k for Australian cargoes, leaving a signiﬁcant gap. In the Far
East, the general cargo segment in the Bohai area saw most prompt cargoes covered as the
Golden Week holiday approaches. On Monday, it was heard that a UMX ﬁxed at 23k to the
Med via Goa, but later the ﬁxture was said to have failed, and market activity was limited.
The Nopac market remained quiet this week, mainly due to reduced cargo volumes, with
not much price exchange observed. In ECI, there are many open vessels. Local iron ore
oﬀers have decreased but remain decent. This week, it was heard that a UMX ﬁxed for ECI
ore to China at as high as 17.5K DOP Local cargo export volumes from WCI remain
generally moderate. A charterer calculated 15K APS for a UMX open in WCI back to fareast
with salt. Some owners still prefer to ballast to SEA this week. The South African market
showed no signiﬁcant change overall. It was heard that a UMX ﬁxed at 22+22K APS from
Safr to the Paciﬁc. In summary, as the May Day Golden Week holiday approaches, market
activity has signiﬁcantly decreased and the market has become quiet. We look forward to
seeing how the market performs going forward.

Capesize Report28th April 2026
PAC: Busy         ATL: Firm
Market Comments
Activity in the Paciﬁc was up from the get-go today, as three majors were seen
in the market. Owners promptly oﬀered very high $13s to $14 range to the
Stanley Point major, who ended up ﬁxing a few mid-May C5 stems, including a
Nuke, with one known to be at $13.50. A Hedland major ﬁxed soon after at
$13.10 for their 14/16 May stem. The Dampier major was reluctant to ﬁx in the
$13s as they were last seen bidding in high $12s for their 17/19 May stem,
before reportedly remaining unﬁxed. The usual operator out of Samarinda
ﬁxed their 04/10 May repositioning stem to Mundra in the low $10s.
Additionally, a South Australian cargo to China for split end May/early June
dates caught the attention of one owner as they oﬀered very high $19s, though
no bid as of yet.After a static start to the week in the South Atlantic, activity
soon picked up on Tuesday as an operator’s South African stem from Richards
Bay to India for 10/19 May was promptly oﬀered high $16s before later ﬁxing,
however rates remain elusive. Additionally, a Japanese operator was seen
bidding $24 vs high $24s on their C17 stem for 15/24 May. Charterers began
amongst the $32.00-50 C3 range across later May dates, whilst one German
operator was seen bidding $31 C3 for their early June stem.  However, owners
remained resilient as oﬀers in the $33.00-75 C3 range remained consistent, and
soon Charterers began bidding at high $32s to $33. A Brazilian stem to
Malaysia ﬁxed in the afternoon for split May/June dates at June C3 equivalent
with a premium. A Korean end user’s fronthaul stem for split May/June dates
will oﬀer insight into the North as it heads to auction tomorrow. West African
stems to the Far East continue to attract vessels stationed in the North as one
vessel was rumoured to have ﬁxed from Nouadhibou to Qingdao for 15/24 May
in the mid $33s, which ran to mid-high $60k basis C9 duration.

Panam ax/Kam sarm ax Report28th April 2026
ATL: FLAT/ SOFTER
PAC: FIRMER
MID EAST: FLATMarket Comments
ATL SHORT

1A - A SLOW START TO THE TRADING WEEK FOR THE TA BUSINESS. ONLY A COUPLE OF FIXTURES
HAVE BEEN REPORTED, WHICH ARE RUNNING MORE OR LESS IN LINE WITH THE INDEX PRINT,
CIRCA 14K. FOR NOW, SUPPLY AND DEMAND APPEAR BALANCED, SUGGESTING ANOTHER FLAT
TRADING WEEK.
2A - A MORE ACTIVE START TO THE WEEK, WITH CHINESE OPERATORS CONTINUING TO ACCOUNT
FOR THE BULK OF THE BUYING. FIXTURES REPORTED ARE RUNNING BACK TO AROUND 25K BKI
DELIVERY ALGECIRAS. SIMILARLY TO THE TA MARKET, NEITHER SUPPLY NOR DEMAND APPEARS
SUFFICIENTLY IMBALANCED TO DRIVE THE MARKET MEANINGFULLY IN EITHER DIRECTION.
P6 - IT APPEARS THOSE WHO LEFT THEIR SHIPS PROMPT HAVE HAD TO REDUCE THEIR NUMBERS
IN ORDER TO SECURE COVER. HOWEVER, VESSELS ARRIVING ON INDEX DATES ARE REPORTED TO
BE FETCHING BETWEEN USD 500 - 750 MORE PER DAY THAN EARLY ARRIVALS, EFFECTIVELY
CREATING A SOMEWHAT TWO-TIERED MARKET IN THE SOUTH.
1A /2A /P6 13900/24579/18715
THE WEEK SO FAR HAS FELT SOMEWHAT DISJOINTED WITH PUBLIC HOLIDAYS FOR MANY ACROSS
THE WORLD, AND GENEVA DRY IN FULL SWING. BUT FOR NOW, CARGO AND VESSEL COUNTS
REMAIN LARGELY BALANCED. HINTING THAT THE WEEK SHOULD TRADE SIDEWAYS MOVING ON
PAC SHORT
THE PACIFIC MARKET HAS SEEN A STRONG AND ACTIVE START TO THE WEEK AS MOMENTUM
CONTINUES TO CARRY THROUGH FROM LAST WEEK. WITH VARIOUS HOLIDAYS IN THE MARKET
DURING THE 2ND HALF OF THIS WEEK AND EARLY NEXT WEEK CHARTERERS ARE KEEN TO FIX
EARLY. INDONESIA IS STILL LEADING THE CHARGE WITH STRONG DEMAND AND EVER IMPROVING
FIXING LEVELS WHILE AUSTRALIA COAL IS FOLLOWING SUIT. NOPAC HAS BEEN FAIRLY SUBDUED
BY COMPARISON WITH FIXING LEVELS ALSO LAGGING COMPARED TO AUSTRALIA. LAST DONE ON
NOPAC IS AROUND MID $17'S BKI CJK, WHILE ON AUSTRALIA WE'VE SEEN MULTIPLE FIXTURES IN
THE MID/HIGH $17'S BKI CJK. ON INDONESIA ROUNDS, OVERAGE LME'S OPEN SOUTH CHINA HAVE
BEEN FIXED AT $20K BACK TO SOUTH CHINA. FFA'S ARE SHOWING IMPROVEMENTS DESPITE A
WEAKER ATLANTIC MARKET AND, AS FIXING LEVELS CONTINUE TO STRENGTHEN, OWNERS ARE
INCREASING THEIR IDEAS AND GENERALLY ASKING $20K+ BKI FOR NOPAC AND $21K+ BKI FOR
AUSTRALIA. WITH JAPAN ON HOLIDAY TOMORROW AND MANY COUNTRIES ON HOLIDAY ON
FRIDAY IT REMAINS TO BE SEEN HOW LONG THE CURRENT LEVELS OF ACTIVITY WILL CONTINUE,
BUT FOR NOW AT LEAST, OWNERS HAVE THE UPPER HAND.

items.parsed_text: Capesize Report28th April 2026 PAC: Busy ATL: Firm Market Comments Activity in the Pacific was up from the get-go today, as three majors were seen in the market. Owners promptly offered very high $13s to $14 range to the Stanley Point major, who ended up fixing a few mid-May C5 stems, including a Nuke, with one known to be at $13.50. A Hedland major fixed soon after at $13.10 for their 14/16 May stem. The Dampier major was reluctant to fix in the $13s as they were last seen bidding in high $12s for their 17/19 May stem, before reportedly remaining unfixed. The usual operator out of Samarinda fixed their 04/10 May repositioning stem to Mundra in the low $10s. Additionally, a South Australian cargo to China for split end May/early June dates caught the attention of one owner as they offered very high $19s, though no bid as of yet.After a static start to the week in the South Atlantic, activity soon picked up on Tuesday as an operator’s South African stem from Richards Bay to India for 10/19 May was promptly offered high $16s before later fixing, however rates remain elusive. Additionally, a Japanese operator was seen bidding $24 vs high $24s on their C17 stem for 15/24 May. Charterers began amongst the $32.00-50 C3 range across later May dates, whilst one German operator was seen bidding $31 C3 for their early June stem. However, owners remained resilient as offers in the $33.00-75 C3 range remained consistent, and soon Charterers began bidding at high $32s to $33. A Brazilian stem to Malaysia fixed in the afternoon for split May/June dates at June C3 equivalent with a premium. A Korean end user’s fronthaul stem for split May/June dates will offer insight into the North as it heads to auction tomorrow. West African stems to the Far East continue to attract vessels stationed in the North as one vessel was rumoured to have fixed from Nouadhibou to Qingdao for 15/24 May in the mid $33s, which ran to mid-high $60k basis C9 duration. items.parsed_text: Panam ax/Kamsarmax Report28th April 2026 ATL: FLAT/ SOFTER PAC: FIRMER MID EAST: FLATMarket Comments ATL SHORT 1A - A SLOW START TO THE TRADING WEEK FOR THE TA BUSINESS. ONLY A COUPLE OF FIXTURES HAVE BEEN REPORTED, WHICH ARE RUNNING MORE OR LESS IN LINE WITH THE INDEX PRINT, CIRCA 14K. FOR NOW, SUPPLY AND DEMAND APPEAR BALANCED, SUGGESTING ANOTHER FLAT TRADING WEEK. 2A - A MORE ACTIVE START TO THE WEEK, WITH CHINESE OPERATORS CONTINUING TO ACCOUNT FOR THE BULK OF THE BUYING. FIXTURES REPORTED ARE RUNNING BACK TO AROUND 25K BKI DELIVERY ALGECIRAS. SIMILARLY TO THE TA MARKET, NEITHER SUPPLY NOR DEMAND APPEARS SUFFICIENTLY IMBALANCED TO DRIVE THE MARKET MEANINGFULLY IN EITHER DIRECTION. P6 - IT APPEARS THOSE WHO LEFT THEIR SHIPS PROMPT HAVE HAD TO REDUCE THEIR NUMBERS IN ORDER TO SECURE COVER. HOWEVER, VESSELS ARRIVING ON INDEX DATES ARE REPORTED TO BE FETCHING BETWEEN USD 500 - 750 MORE PER DAY THAN EARLY ARRIVALS, EFFECTIVELY CREATING A SOMEWHAT TWO-TIERED MARKET IN THE SOUTH. 1A /2A /P6 13900/24579/18715 THE WEEK SO FAR HAS FELT SOMEWHAT DISJOINTED WITH PUBLIC HOLIDAYS FOR MANY ACROSS THE WORLD, AND GENEVA DRY IN FULL SWING. BUT FOR NOW, CARGO AND VESSEL COUNTS REMAIN LARGELY BALANCED. HINTING THAT THE WEEK SHOULD TRADE SIDEWAYS MOVING ON PAC SHORT THE PACIFIC MARKET HAS SEEN A STRONG AND ACTIVE START TO THE WEEK AS MOMENTUM CONTINUES TO CARRY THROUGH FROM LAST WEEK. WITH VARIOUS HOLIDAYS IN THE MARKET DURING THE 2ND HALF OF THIS WEEK AND EARLY NEXT WEEK CHARTERERS ARE KEEN TO FIX EARLY. INDONESIA IS STILL LEADING THE CHARGE WITH STRONG DEMAND AND EVER IMPROVING FIXING LEVELS WHILE AUSTRALIA COAL IS FOLLOWING SUIT. NOPAC HAS BEEN FAIRLY SUBDUED BY COMPARISON WITH FIXING LEVELS ALSO LAGGING COMPARED TO AUSTRALIA. LAST DONE ON NOPAC IS AROUND MID $17'S BKI CJK, WHILE ON AUSTRALIA WE'VE SEEN MULTIPLE FIXTURES IN THE MID/HIGH $17'S BKI CJK. ON INDONESIA ROUNDS, OVERAGE LME'S OPEN SOUTH CHINA HAVE BEEN FIXED AT $20K BACK TO SOUTH CHINA. FFA'S ARE SHOWING IMPROVEMENTS DESPITE A WEAKER ATLANTIC MARKET AND, AS FIXING LEVELS CONTINUE TO STRENGTHEN, OWNERS ARE INCREASING THEIR IDEAS AND GENERALLY ASKING $20K+ BKI FOR NOPAC AND $21K+ BKI FOR AUSTRALIA. WITH JAPAN ON HOLIDAY TOMORROW AND MANY COUNTRIES ON HOLIDAY ON FRIDAY IT REMAINS TO BE SEEN HOW LONG THE CURRENT LEVELS OF ACTIVITY WILL CONTINUE, BUT FOR NOW AT LEAST, OWNERS HAVE THE UPPER HAND. However, output stood 5.3% below the same period last year. Trading Commentary Cape Routes The c5 market moved higher again today as the may contract traded a few times up at 13.30 where it closed offered on. The june had some enquiry but not trades to report, closing valued at 13.10. The c3 also ticked up again today as the may traded at 33.40 in the morning session, closing slightly lower valued at 33.25. The june also had alot of enquiry but no trades reported. Cape The Cape FFA curve rallied higher in response to a firmer Pacific market, combined with a tighter south Atlantic market. The biggest move was on the May contract with 35350 paid, followed by the June up to a high of 34000. The May v June spread continued to widen and strengthen with 1750 paid. Q3 was supported on open with volume being paid up to 30600, before being sold back down to 28900. Similarly the trading range on Q4 was 29800-30300 but with sporadic liquidity, whereas the Cal27 traded up to 25900 during the morning session, then sold down to 25550 during the afternoon sell-off. Activity on the Cal28 was limited with 22900 paid, then sold back down to 22650. PMX PMX opened slightly higher than yesterday’s close, with good volume seen across the curve. May traded down to a low of 18800 before being paid up to 19600, finishing the day around 19100. Jun saw less movement, trading in a range of 19200–19700 and closing at 19500. Aug was paid at 18800, which saw the Jun/Aug spread trade at 800. Q3 bounced around 18500 to 18900, while Q4 held a tighter range between 17250 and 17400. Further out, Cal27 saw participation today, trading around 14650. SMX + HANDY The Smx Asia Index cast doubt over the strength of paper with a modest +10 on the Avg TC. This somewhat set the tone of sellers being more eager to transact, though in the morning session positivity from the bigger vessel sizes largely offset the negative concerns on Smx. items.parsed_text: Handysize/Supramax Report28th April 2026 63,500 Atlantic: SOFTER Pacific: FLAT 38,000 Atlantic: FLAT Pacific: FLAT Market Comments ATLANTIC: In the Handysize Continent market, activity remains subdued with little fresh enquiry thus far. Fixing levels are at around USD 9,000 for a transatlantic voyage, a similar level to last week. For the Supramax and Ultramax sizes, rates have held firm from last week, supported by a relatively tight tonnage list. We have seen a 63k deadweight vessel fix a trip from ARAG range to East Coast Mexico on subjects at USD 12,000. In the Handysize Mediterranean market, rates have remained flat as the week opened with limited fresh enquiries. We saw a 39k deadweight vessel rate a trip from the East Mediterranean to Spore/Japan range at USD 16,000, which is the same rating as last week. We saw a 35k deadweight vessel fix a trip from Çanakkale to Florida at USD 10,750 (plus USD 150,000 ILOHC). For the larger sizes, tonnage lists remain long and enquiry limited. Fixing levels are at around USD 10,000 for a transatlantic voyage, a firmer level than last week. The Handysize East Coast South America (ECSA) market is still hot with healthy demand, thus we are continuing to see better rates. For the Ultramax size, fronthaul numbers are sitting at USD 17,000 + 700k GBB. Meanwhile in West Africa, there is limited demand and the tonnage list is building. The Handysize US Gulf market has opened particularly slowly this week as both Owners and Charterers try to gauge current market direction. Underlying sentiment feels quietly constructive, with Owners pushing firmer ideas. There has been limited fresh enquiry, however we suspect Charterers are keeping some orders off market until later in the week. Tonnage count remains stable, possibly marginally tighter than last week. Whereas on the Supramax and Ultramax US Gulf market it has been a rather quiet start to the week. We are still seeing some inter-caribs business present but less transatlantic enquiry. Fronthaul orders are building up for mid May dates with grains especially, but nothing has been concluded yet. We feel the market is a tick firmer for the fronthauls as the market aligns closer to the transatlantic levels which are coming down from the upper 20k levels. PACIFIC: The Pacific market was quiet this week. Most prompt cargoes have been covered, but there are still some spot vessels left. In the Southeast Asian coal market, the India direction was less hot than last week. A UMX open in Chittagong could not see 20k DOP for an Indo/India run this week, marking a downward adjustment compared to last week. For the Indo/China direction, bids for an SMX based in Singapore were around mid 15k, also lower. There are still a few Indo/Thai cargoes waiting to be covered, with rates showing no significant change. It was heard that a UMX open in the Philippines fixed at 21.5k for an Indo/Thai run. Aussie cargoes generally felt that tonnage supply was ample. Offers this week decreased by 1-2k compared to last week. It is currently heard that a UMX open in Chittagong can see around mid 16k for an Aussie RV, but owners' ideas remain high, with most owners wanting 18-19k for Australian cargoes, leaving a significant gap. In the Far East, the general cargo segment in the Bohai area saw most prompt cargoes covered as the Golden Week holiday approaches. On Monday, it was heard that a UMX fixed at 23k to the Med via Goa, but later the fixture was said to have failed, and market activity was limited. The Nopac market remained quiet this week, mainly due to reduced cargo volumes, with not much price exchange observed. In ECI, there are many open vessels. Local iron ore offers have decreased but remain decent. This week, it was heard that a UMX fixed for ECI ore to China at as high as 17.5K DOP Local cargo export volumes from WCI remain generally moderate. A charterer calculated 15K APS for a UMX open in WCI back to fareast with salt. Some owners still prefer to ballast to SEA this week. The South African market showed no significant change overall. It was heard that a UMX fixed at 22+22K APS from Safr to the Pacific. In summary, as the May Day Golden Week holiday approaches, market activity has significantly decreased and the market has become quiet. We look forward to seeing how the market performs going forward. ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场周二整体小幅走强，各Baltic指数全线上涨，其中Capesize领涨（BCI+22点至4304），Panamax和Supramax分别微升9点和2点。尽管Capesize太平洋市场受三家矿商活跃支撑表现强劲，大西洋C3航线却因买卖盘价差扩大而呈现僵持；Panamax则呈现太平洋坚挺、大西洋疲软的分叉格局。FFA曲线显示近月合约（尤其是Cape May26）获得买盘支撑，但远期Cal27-30预期继续走弱，反映市场对中期需求持谨慎态度。

sections.title: 市场结构
sections.content: Capesize太平洋市场由三大矿商领衔走强，C5航线涨至$13.20，西澳至中国航线询盘活跃；大西洋C3则因南美和西非货盘稀疏而横盘。Panamax亚洲持续优于大西洋，印尼和澳洲煤炭航线成交活跃，个别老龄船固定于$17,250/日。Supramax和Handysize整体平稳，印度洋和东南亚有零星需求。

sections.title: 干散货信号
sections.content: FFA曲线近月走强与现货指数背离：Cape May26固定$34,700（高于现货$35,536），反映短期情绪乐观；但Cal27-30持续贴水，Cape Cal27报$25,500/25,550，远低于即期水平。Supramax和Handysize的FFA亦显示远期看跌趋势，暗示市场对中长期基本面存隐忧。铁矿石和炼焦煤价格持平，未提供新增方向指引。

sections.title: 交易关注
sections.content: 建议关注：Capesize大西洋C3航线的买卖盘博弈（买方$32 vs 卖方$34），若后续货盘跟进则有望突破；Panamax太平洋航线印尼及澳洲煤炭的持续活跃度；Supramax印度洋定期租成交（$22,000+补贴$220,000），反映区域需求旺盛。远期曲线的贴水结构提供跨期套利机会。

market_watch: Capesize太平洋C5航线维持坚挺，关注三大矿商后续货盘动态
Panamax大西洋P2A指数回落$307，与太平洋走势分化
Supramax印度洋定期租成交活跃，ASTRO GRUMIUM号录得$22,000+补贴$220,000
FFA曲线Cal27-30持续贴水，远期预期偏弱
Baltic各指数全线小幅上扬，整体情绪边际改善

route_focus.view: 大西洋C3微涨至$33.118，但买卖盘价差显著（买方$32 vs 卖方$34），活跃度仍低。西非至远东有少量传言成交，中期方向待五一假期后货盘跟进确认。短期支撑位$32，阻力位$34。
跨大西洋航线物理市场报$13,000-15,000（租家vs船东），即期期租平均值$14,584。较P2A（远东）大幅贴水，反映大西洋需求疲软，短期缺乏催化剂。FFA曲线P1A期限结构亦呈远月贴水格局。
Handysize Skaw-Passero至Rio de Janeiro-Recalada航线报$7,650，下跌$236。大西洋南向航线走弱明显，与北向HS3（$23,211,+161）形成鲜明对比，南北分化格局延续。
